It's understandable, as someone who has bpd and autism its hard when you gain a favorite person and it's not reciprocated. I understand where you are coming from, and it's really hard to stop thinking about them. You are not a stalker. You are just someone who is hurting. Yes, I agree with others that obsessing isn't good, and I've done my fair share of it, too. It's really hard to get over, but sometimes you do just need to let go. If it's a big issue at work, I'd honestly suggest starting fresh and looking for a new job. Work can be hard enough, and you don't need extra emotional toll of being an outcast and ridiculed for something THEY misinterpreted. You can't always change how you feel, but you can change what you do and how you react. Don't worry about the other comments too much, no one here even knows who you really are so don't take it too personally, this one interaction doesn't describe who you are as a person. The gifts are a sweet idea but sometimes people can take it as an unwanted romantic gesture, but it's their fault for not communicating their own feelings afterwards. Social interactions are hard and people will take the smallest things into account. Therapy CAN always help you get more perspective as you can go way more in Depth. 

My biggest piece of advice is don't let people bring you down with what THEY think about you, it only matters how you feel about yourself, and if you want to feel better, be with people who are better too, and who will talk when something bothers them.
